newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-KEY DORTMUND TRIO PULL OUT OF SEMIFINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KEY DORTMUND TRIO PULL OUT OF SEMIFINAL.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund will be without their main striking duo Stephane Chapuisat and Karlheinz Riedle as well as experienced defender Juergen Kohler for Wednesday's European Cup semifinal against Manchester United.

The German champions had hoped to get the trio fit in time for the first leg. But club doctor Werner Bastians passed on the bad news to coach Ottmar Hitzfeld on Tuesday evening, leaving the trainer to reconsider his line-up completely.
"No team in the world would be able to cope with this without it having some effect," Hitzfeld said. "Our supporters really have to support us now and make up for the missing players."
Kohler, the most experienced defender in the German game, had flown to Munich to see one of Europe's leading sports doctors in a bid to recover from an ankle injury.
Fellow German international forward Riedle, who has been having treatment on a groin injury, has been complaining of pains at the back of his neck. Swiss Chapuisat has back problems.

Hitzfeld is expected to field German international Heiko Herrlich, who has also just returned from injury, and midfielder Rene Tretschok up front. Martin Kree will probably replace Kohler at the back.

By contrast Manchester United were able to report a fully-fit team on Tuesday. With Dortmund missing eight squad members and forced to field a second-choice team, the English champions must be confident of getting a good result to take back to Old Trafford for the second leg in two weeks.

In addition to the injured trio of internationals, Dortmund libero Matthias Sammer is suspended. Brazilian Julio Cesar and fellow defender Rene Schneider, midfielder Steffen Freund and striker Ibrahim Tanko are also all unfit.
"We are going to lift ourselves despite the problems," Hitzfeld said. "The game is a highlight for every player and the club. We are in the spotlight of European football."

Dortmund will have to play midfielder Andy Moeller despite the fact that he is also struggling with injury. The German international has been to see a leading physiotherapist in recent day because of muscle pains in his legs.
Dortmund (probable): Stefan Klos, Wolfgang Feiersinger, Stefan Reuter, Martin Kree, Lars Ricken, Paul Lambert, Paulo Sousa, Joerg Heinrich, Andy Moeller, Heiko Herrlich, Rene Tretschok
